transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. Before we dive in, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Yeah, thanks, Dr. Lee. I guess the main thing is work stuff. I’m a supervisor in sales, and lately I’ve been making these... I don’t know, kind of careless mistakes on reports. Like copying the wrong numbers over from the team dashboard, or missing a line in a procedure I was supposed to check.

I do try to go back over things, so it’s frustrating because I think I’ve reviewed it, and then someone points it out. It’s not huge every time, but it’s happening enough that I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Have you noticed any issues with your sleep lately, such as snoring, gasping for air, or feeling excessively tired during the day even after a full night's sleep?

Um… not that I’ve really noticed, no. I mean, I don’t think I snore much—at least nobody’s mentioned it to me—and I haven’t woken up gasping or anything like that.

I do get tired sometimes, but I kind of assumed that was just normal work and life stuff. I wouldn’t say I feel wiped out even after a full night’s sleep, if that makes sense.
Have you had trouble with careless mistakes, forgetfulness, or losing focus like this since childhood or your school years, or is this a new pattern that started recently?

Yeah… I think it’s been around a long time, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound like I was some terrible kid or anything, but my mom still brings up notes from teachers in elementary school.

Stuff like I’d rush through my work and make mistakes, lose homework, talk out of turn… and I guess I had a hard time staying in my seat unless someone reminded me. So, no, I don’t think it’s completely new. It’s just more noticeable now with work.
